requirement:
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.

An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.

Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
rationale:
**Judgment:** `requirements.references.anchors` is satisfied. I found no unacknowledged gaps. The one point that could be read as a gap is the skill-guidance obligation, discussed at the end.

## Implementation

Each obligation in the requirement text has marked `{impl}` code:

- **Option-line syntax.**
  - `definition_blocks` and `option_line` in `src/lib.rs` read option lines only immediately after the opening fence of a `{req}` or `{example}`, stopping at the first non-option line. Terms are skipped.
  - `DefinitionBlock` and `DefinitionOption` carry the parsed options.
- **Anchor parsing.**
  - `collect_definitions` in `src/evidence.rs` maps `:impl:` to an impl edge, accepted on a `{req}` only.
  - It maps `:test:` to a test edge, accepted on a `{req}` or an `{example}`.
  - Any other option, and an empty path, is a validation error that names the definition and the line.
  - `Anchor::parse` splits `path#selector`.
- **Option lines excluded from text.** `without_options` removes them from the definition text, from `raw_lines` (the requirements input text), and from rendering. `replace_definitions` and `preprocess_book` render the body from `text_start`.
- **Resolution and permission.** `Anchor::resolve` goes through `OutlineCache::parse`, which does the permitted-read check, and then `ParsedSource::resolve`, which does the selector resolution under `outline_selectors`.
- **Coverage.**
  - `validate_references` requires that some evidence input selects the anchored node or one of its ancestors. `AnchorTarget.nodes` lists the node and its ancestors, and `InputRange.node` records what each input selected.
  - An unresolved anchor produces a validation error naming the definition, the anchor path and the declaration source.
- **Authoring reports before inference.** `AssessmentSources::prepare` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` resolves every anchor. It fails with `<name>: cannot read :<kind>: anchor <path>`, keeping `PermissionDenied` for denied paths. Anchors turn into outline-input selectors, so the evidence covers them. This happens before any inference.
- **Edges and discoverability.**
  - The `references` tool in `src/authoring/tools.rs` reports anchors as impl/test sites with a null line.
  - `DefinitionEdges::current` in `src/index.rs` uses anchors to group inputs on the detail page.
- **Skill guidance.** `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` is anchored with `:impl:` from the declaration. It explains the anchor syntax and says "Do not anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such as a comment attached to the Rust item…". That carries out the "SHOULD NOT / skills MUST give this direction" sentence.

## Tests

The tests cover the main points of the design space:

- `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable` (`src/evidence.rs`) checks:
  - a section-only input does not cover a whole-file anchor;
  - an unresolvable `:test: missing.sh` is a validation error;
  - an example `:test:` anchor is covered;
  - option lines are not part of the text;
  - changing the anchored file makes the evidence stale.
- `selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor` covers a sibling input failing, a node, ancestor and root input succeeding, and a missing selector failing.
- `unsupported_and_empty_options_are_validation_errors` covers an unknown option, an empty `:impl:`, and `:impl:` on an example.
- `requirements_inputs_omit_option_lines` and `anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text` cover:
  - the text and requirements-input exclusion;
  - the "immediately after the fence" rule (a later `:test:` line stays body text);
  - options on a nested example inside a requirement;
  - non-rendering.
- `anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs`, `unreadable_or_denied_anchors_fail_before_inference` (missing file and a denied path) and `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` (selector anchors) cover the authoring-side behavior.
- `references_report_anchors_as_file_or_node_sites` covers the `references` tool, including omitting a denied anchor.
- The index and detail-page tests cover grouping and "no option text rendered".

## Reservation

Only `habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` states the anchor direction. `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` does not repeat it, but it explicitly defers to the `habeas-requirements` guidance for directive syntax. I judged that sufficient, but a stricter reading of "bundled agent skills" could require the direction in the bootstrap skill as well.

:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} targets

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under {cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git` and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
A source item MUST choose its references for each candidate definition by this
procedure, and MAY carry several:
1. If the item is a test or test helper designed to verify the definition, it
MUST use `{test}`.
2. Otherwise, if fulfilling the definition depends on the item, it MUST use
`{impl}`. For code, this means it makes a decision, performs a check,
produces an output, or handles a case the definition specifies. For a type,
this means the definition constrains its shape: fields, variants, serialized
form, or validation.
3. Otherwise, if the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the
definition changes, it MUST use `{cite}`.
4. If the item carries no reference after applying steps 1 to 3 to every
definition, it MUST cite the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, justifying why the item
exists.

:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, `references`, and `inputs`. `references` MUST be the reference-set digest defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
:::{req} evidence_coverage

For every `{impl}` and `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a requirement or example declaration, the evidence file for the referenced requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line. A `{cite}` reference MUST NOT require coverage; it is discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference with its role, full name, source file, and line number.
